_about: Plain-English wording for Decisions 30 and 31. Single source of truth for the API (serving/app.py), the dashboard (dashboard/scoring.py) and the public site (website/public/assets/reasons.js). Each detail has wording for when the applicant's value is lower or higher than the typical applicant's. Wording describes what the model links to risk; it never claims cause and never mentions the review cutoff.

refer.title: Why this application was referred for review
refer.intro: The application has been passed to a person to review; it has not been declined. The details that counted most against it were:
refer.link: The model links each of these to a higher chance of falling behind on repayments.
refer.none: No single detail stood out; it was the combination of details that the model linked to a higher chance of falling behind on repayments.

pass.title: Why this application was not referred
pass.intro: The model did not flag this application for review. The details that counted most in its favour were:
pass.none: No single detail stood out; the details taken together were not flagged.
pass.against_intro: Details the model linked to higher risk, though not enough to flag it:

refer: Check these details are correct. If any are wrong, ask for them to be corrected before the review.
A referral is not a decline: a reviewer looks at the whole application.
This explains how the model scored these details on synthetic data. It is not financial advice.
pass: This explains how the model scored these details on synthetic data. It is not financial advice.

method.new: Each detail was compared with a typical applicant by changing that one detail and re-scoring with the model.
method.existing: Each detail was compared with a typical customer by changing that one detail and re-scoring with the model.

review.heading: Risk officer review required
review.data_input: Some details are unusual compared with the data the model learned from: {issues}. A risk officer will check them before anything is decided. If any are wrong, ask for them to be corrected.
review.missing_information: Applicants with a full credit file are a group where the model is known to be less reliable: it rarely marks them as high risk, even though some do fall behind. This application scored among the highest {top}% for that group, so a risk officer will review it.
review.overreliance: The recommendation rests mainly on one detail of the application, so a risk officer will check it rather than rely on the model alone.
review.next_step: A risk officer will review this application before anything is decided. It has not been declined.
review.data_only_intro: Rather than list individual details, here is how past customers like you fared in the data the model learned from.
review.data_intro: Past customers like you, in the data the model learned from:

issues.out_of_range: {label} of {value}, outside the range seen in that data
issues.thin_long_history: a limited credit file but {months} of credit history
issues.full_short_history: a full credit file but only {months} of credit history
issues.commitments_vs_income: existing commitments of {obligations} a month against an income of {income}

data.band: Among {n} past customers {condition}, about {k} in every 1,000 fell 90 days or more behind on repayments.
data.overall: Across all {n} past customers the model learned from, about {k} in every 1,000 fell 90 days or more behind on repayments.
data.segment: Among {n} past customers with a full credit file, about {k} in every 1,000 fell 90 days or more behind on repayments.
data.segment_top: Among the {top}% of them the model scored highest, about {k} in every 1,000 did.
data.method: These figures count the {n} past customers in the model's training data, in groups of at least {min_group}. They describe what happened to similar customers, not what will happen to you.

error_labels.missing_information: Known blind spot (information the model lacks)

genre_reasons.features: Features-based explanation: it helps people spot a wrong input (Belton et al. 2025, Decision 7).
genre_reasons.data_centric: Data-centric explanation, no per-detail attributions: they can hide a model error of this kind (Belton et al. 2025, Decision 7). Human review triggered.
genre_reasons.combination: Combination explanation: appropriate when no error type is detected (Decision 7).

data_input.name: Inputs consistent with the training data
data_input.ok: All inputs inside the training ranges and consistent with each other.

missing_information.name: Known blind spot: full credit file
missing_information.triggered: Full credit file, score at or above the group's {pct}th-percentile line ({line}).
missing_information.ok: Full credit file, score below the group's {pct}th-percentile line ({line}).

overreliance.name: Recommendation rests on one detail
overreliance.triggered: {name}: setting it alone to typical would change the recommendation, and it carries most of the total effect.
overreliance.ok: No single detail decides the recommendation.

officer.divergence_note: The model's recommendation is below the review threshold, but a check requires a person to review it.

record.approver_note: Not recorded: the approval gate does not capture approver identity (Decision 23).
lineage: Decision 27: champion {model_version}, promoted on validity grounds
Decision 27: business cutoff {cutoff}, PD at or above it refers for review
Decision 30: plain-English reasons, one input at a time against a typical applicant
Decision 31: error-type checks, explanation genre and risk officer flag (rules {rules_version})
